knowledge_events: SE-0061-02-05T07:20:00 | direct_delivery | source=pc_wei_tang | recipient=canon_hiruzen | Wei personally delivered a written proposal titled 'Proposal for a Permanent Six-Man Special Operations Squad'. Requested role: squad commander. Requested strength: six permanent members. Any approved roster is intended as the same permanent general-purpose special-operations unit for capture, assassination, infiltration, reconnaissance, tracking, sabotage, defense, and direct combat, training and deploying together over years. Ordered roster preferences: 1) Wei Tang / Ensui Nara / Aoba Yamashiro / Yugao Uzuki / Hayate Gekko / Hoheto Hyūga; 2) Wei Tang / Suzaku Nara / Muta Aburame / Hoheto Hyūga / Tekuno Kanden / Hayama Shirakumo; 3) Wei Tang / Kosuke Maruboshi / Zaji / Tekuno Kanden / Hayama Shirakumo / Hoheto Hyūga; 4) Wei Tang / Daikoku Funeno / Suzume / Tekuno Kanden / Hayama Shirakumo / Hoheto Hyūga. Wei requests command's opinion on which choices it agrees with, replacements, whether he is overestimating or underestimating candidates, whether any candidate should remain in the current assignment, and overlooked shinobi. He asks that the finalized team be kept together permanently. He states the first choice can become elite quickly, the second or third can be built, and the fourth is the lowest permanent roster he is willing to accept and a test of command and development. Delivery itself grants no approval, assignment change, or candidate commitment.

SE-0061-02-05T07:22:00 | direct_dialogue | source=pc_wei_tang | recipient=canon_hiruzen | Wei requests immediate discussion of the proposal and specifically asks Hiruzen to identify operational problems, replacement candidates, misjudged capabilities, and duty conflicts. Wei clarifies that he still intends to take the 09:00 Team Fujin Genin assignment even if a permanent special-operations squad is later approved, meaning he is asking to carry responsibility for both teams rather than replace one with the other.

SE-0061-02-05T07:45:00 | direct_dialogue | source=canon_hiruzen | recipient=pc_wei_tang | Hiruzen gives a provisional command assessment, not authorization. He considers the permanent six-person general-purpose special-operations concept defensible but requires personnel availability and duty review before approval. He says maintaining Team Fujin concurrently is not a raw command-span problem, but it creates unavoidable scheduling and physical-presence conflicts; Genin instructor duty remains real, and mission priority, deputy authority, and coverage must be formalized before dual command can be approved. Roster assessment: the first roster is the strongest immediate tactical package but the hardest institutionally; Yugao is active ANBU, Aoba serves intelligence, and Wei plus Yugao plus Hayate overconcentrates sword-assault capability for a general-purpose unit. Ensui and Hoheto are strong selections. The second roster is Hiruzen's preferred starting point for authorization because Suzaku, Muta, Hoheto, Tekuno, and Hayama are complementary and create fewer permanent-assignment conflicts; Hayama is a credible field deputy. The third roster is stronger than Wei labels it because Kosuke's Genin rank understates his veteran field capability; Zaji is a narrower developmental sensor. The fourth roster is least attractive in exact form because Daikoku and Suzume are Academy instructors; stripping both teaching posts merely to create a deliberately weaker team is a poor institutional trade. Hiruzen's corrections: Hayate is not a dedicated pursuit or tracking specialist; Hoheto is more than overwatch; Hayama and Kosuke are underestimated; Aoba is useful intelligence support but not freely disposable from that function. Before naming outside candidates, Hiruzen wants a personnel availability check and says cross-swaps from Wei's own lists, especially Muta or Tekuno into a modified first roster, deserve consideration. No roster, second team, transfer, or permanent command is approved by this discussion.

SE-0061-02-05T07:46:00 | direct_dialogue | source=pc_wei_tang | recipient=canon_hiruzen | Wei asks Hiruzen to name the five candidates Hiruzen considers best suited to serve permanently beside Wei in the proposed six-person general-purpose special-operations squad.

SE-0061-02-05T07:55:00 | direct_dialogue | source=canon_hiruzen | recipient=pc_wei_tang | Hiruzen recommends, as his current preferred five-person complement to Wei rather than an authorization, Ensui Nara, Muta Aburame, Hoheto Hyūga, Tekuno Kanden, and Hayama Shirakumo. Rationale: Ensui supplies high-level restraint and battlefield control; Muta supplies distributed reconnaissance, tracking, and counter-surveillance; Hoheto supplies Byakugan reconnaissance, tracking, close-range defense, and a second independent sensing modality; Tekuno supplies traps, explosives, field engineering, sabotage, denial, and prepared-ground capability; Hayama supplies high-level secondary combat and credible field leadership, making him Hiruzen's preferred deputy candidate if Wei is also responsible for Team Fujin. Hiruzen says Muta and Hoheto are complementary rather than redundant because they observe and search in different ways. He would keep Aoba primarily available to Intelligence and Yugao in ANBU absent a stronger transfer case, and would not pull both Daikoku and Suzume from Academy teaching. Suzaku Nara is Hiruzen's first restraint/control alternate if Ensui is unavailable, and Kosuke Maruboshi is a high-value veteran alternate if roster needs change. No roster, transfer, second team, or permanent command is approved; formal personnel availability, duty-conflict review, and dual-command coverage remain required.

SE-0061-02-05T07:56:00 | direct_dialogue | source=pc_wei_tang | recipient=canon_hiruzen | Wei asks Hiruzen to search beyond every candidate in Wei's original proposal and identify whether any other Konoha shinobi would improve the permanent six-person special-operations structure.

SE-0061-02-05T08:15:00 | direct_dialogue | source=canon_hiruzen | recipient=pc_wei_tang | After reviewing outside candidates, Hiruzen revises his provisional default complement to Ensui Nara, Hana Inuzuka, Hoheto Hyūga, Tekuno Kanden, and Hayama Shirakumo beside Wei. Hana is the clearest improvement because she combines elite tracking, infiltration, investigation, field medicine, poison stabilization, and competent combat without a saved permanent office assignment; with Hoheto already providing high-grade reconnaissance and sensing, Hana broadens the team's survivability more than a second dedicated tracker does. Muta Aburame remains a superior mission-profile alternate when counter-surveillance, covert tracking, or Aburame methods are central. Kurenai Yuhi is Hiruzen's strongest outside specialist alternative for genjutsu, tracking, and secondary command, but is not his default because she does not solve the team's medical gap. Inoichi Yamanaka is an exceptional sensor, investigator, communicator, and mental-technique option, but Hiruzen considers his telepathic network capability more valuable as a flexible village asset unless a mission profile specifically requires him inside the permanent cell. Ibiki Morino is better retained as interrogation and intelligence exploitation support than as a permanent field member. Shizune would solve the medical problem at a higher medical tier but is currently traveling with Tsunade and is therefore not treated as an available permanent candidate. Anko Mitarashi is a capable tracker and covert capture/assassination operative but overlaps more of the team's existing pursuit and direct-action functions than Hana does. No roster, transfer, second team, or permanent command is approved; the recommendation remains subject to formal personnel availability and duty-conflict review.

SE-0061-02-05T08:16:00 | direct_dialogue | source=pc_wei_tang | recipient=canon_hiruzen | Wei endorses Hiruzen's revised permanent-core recommendation of Ensui Nara, Hana Inuzuka, Hoheto Hyūga, Tekuno Kanden, and Hayama Shirakumo beside Wei and asks command to begin formal personnel availability and duty-conflict review for those five. Wei also states his intended future mission profile for the proposed unit: S-rank work including infiltration of Root, operations attacking Akatsuki targets, and high-profile bounty-target missions. This is a request for future mission employment and does not itself create a mission order, target authorization, transfer, or team.

SE-0061-02-05T08:25:00 | direct_dialogue | source=canon_hiruzen | recipient=pc_wei_tang | Hiruzen accepts the revised five for formal personnel availability and duty-conflict review but does not approve the team, transfers, dual command, or any mission. He states that S-rank classification and targets remain command decisions rather than a standing entitlement of the proposed squad. Root is an internal Konoha security matter: any infiltration, surveillance, or hostile operation against Root or its personnel would require explicit direct Hokage authorization and compartmented orders; Wei is not authorized to investigate or attack Root independently. Operations against Akatsuki require actionable intelligence and a specific lawful mission order, and high-profile bounty targets must be Konoha-sanctioned targets rather than freelance bounty hunting. Hiruzen says the aggressive profile is compatible with why a balanced permanent unit could be useful, but the squad would first need lawful formation, demonstrated coordination, a deputy/coverage structure compatible with Team Fujin, and mission-specific authorization.

SE-0061-02-05T08:55:00 | academy_checkin | source=konoha_academy_assignment_staff | recipient=pc_wei_tang | Wei checks in for Team Fujin and receives the available official assignment material. The packet confirms Wei Tang as the intended Jonin instructor; Genin Kai Tang, Riku Hyūga, and Mei Arakawa; Mei as acting field leader when the instructor is absent; and the saved role outline for the three Genin. Riku and Mei are physically present in the assignment hall. Kai is not present there. Staff do not provide Wei a verified reason or alternate location for Kai's absence.

SE-0061-02-05T09:00:00 | institutional_assignment | source=konoha_academy_village_assignment | recipient=pc_wei_tang | The scheduled village assignment process takes effect. Because lawful Konoha assignment authority, the committed roster, the effective time, and Wei's previously communicated acceptance are satisfied, Team Fujin becomes an active Konoha Genin team with Wei Tang as Jonin instructor; Kai Tang, Riku Hyūga, and Mei Arakawa as the three Genin; and Mei as acting field leader when Wei is absent. Kai remains physically absent from the assignment hall at the moment of activation. The assignment does not create a team doctrine, alter personal trust or reputation, or approve the separate special-operations squad.

SE-0061-02-05T09:03:00 | direct_request_and_dispatch | source=pc_wei_tang | recipient=konoha_academy_assignment_staff | Wei requests that Academy staff send word to Kai Tang concerning his missed Team Fujin assignment. Staff accept the request and dispatch word through ordinary village channels. Delivery to Kai and any response are not verified during the following assessment period.

SE-0061-02-05T09:45:00 | direct_observation | source=char.riku_hyuga+char.mei_arakawa | recipient=pc_wei_tang | Wei completes a short non-doctrinal baseline practical assessment with Riku Hyūga and Mei Arakawa on an adjacent Academy practice yard. The diagnostic emphasizes ordinary movement, weapons, awareness, judgment, and paired objective work rather than signature-technique expenditure. Riku visibly demonstrates strong physicality, staff handling, tactical awareness, and terrain-oriented judgment. Mei visibly demonstrates high movement precision, stealth, thrown-tool handling, sensory discipline, and tactical control. Their individual judgment is sound, but they do not yet possess rehearsed shared timing. Kai's absence prevents a complete Team Fujin assessment. The short diagnostic grants no team doctrine, promotion, relationship-score change, permanent technique mastery, or measurable skill-point change.

SE-0061-02-05T09:52:00 | institutional_message_delivery | source=konoha_academy_assignment_staff | recipient=char.kai | The Academy notice concerning Kai Tang's missed Team Fujin assignment reaches Kai at Sword Manor through the ordinary village channel previously dispatched at 09:03. The notice informs him that Team Fujin activated at 09:00 under Wei Tang and directs him to report to the Academy. The delivery itself does not establish why Kai missed the original assignment.

SE-0061-02-05T10:10:00 | direct_observation | source=char.kai | recipient=pc_wei_tang | Kai Tang reports to the Academy after receiving the assignment notice. Wei can directly verify that Kai is now physically present with Team Fujin. The reason for Kai's absence at 09:00 remains unverified.

SE-0061-02-05T10:50:00 | direct_observation | source=char.riku_hyuga+char.mei_arakawa | recipient=pc_wei_tang | Wei completes controlled individual chakra and signature-technique demonstrations with Riku and Mei. Riku demonstrates Eight-Point Fault with Byakugan-supported observation: eight small registered terrain points are used to funnel movement through precise local shifts rather than large-volume Earth Release. Mei demonstrates False Opening as a subtle single-detail perceptual manipulation and Frost Senbon as a precise Ice Release projectile volley. The demonstrations are controlled training uses and establish observed capability, not new mastery or doctrine.

SE-0061-02-05T11:35:00 | direct_observation | source=char.riku_hyuga+char.mei_arakawa | recipient=pc_wei_tang | Wei completes a harder controlled paired capture-and-defense pressure drill with Riku and Mei. Under scaled instructor pressure, their early rounds show independent reactions and duplicated movement; later rounds show better lane sharing, timing, and complementary use of Riku's anchoring presence and Mei's angle control. Their best later sequence produces a valid drill containment/tag at the imposed training pace, but this is not equivalent to defeating a Jonin in combat. The block is too short to create an integer skill/mastery increase, promotion, relationship-score change, or adopted team doctrine. Kai is present to observe but remains without an equivalent practical assessment.

SE-0061-02-05T11:40:00 | direct_dialogue | source=pc_wei_tang+char.kai | recipient=pc_wei_tang | Wei asks Kai why he was late for Team Fujin's assignment. Kai says he had been training at Sword Manor, lost track of the time, and failed to check the clock even though he knew the assignment was that morning. He does not claim an emergency or conflicting order and accepts that the miss was his mistake. This is Kai's account to Wei, not independently verified evidence of the earlier offscreen cause.

SE-0061-02-05T12:15:00 | direct_observation | source=char.kai | recipient=pc_wei_tang | Wei completes Kai's individual baseline assessment. Kai's strongest visible areas are sword handling and ordinary movement. His tactical judgment, thrown-tool handling, and team coordination are much less developed than Riku's and Mei's. Kai demonstrates no field-ready ninjutsu or signature technique during the assessment. His authoritative current repertoire contains no field-usable techniques, so Wei receives no observed evidence supporting the assignment packet's air-control role beyond the institutional label itself. The block creates no permanent doctrine, promotion, relationship-score change, or integer capability increase.

SE-0061-02-05T13:15:00 | direct_observation | source=char.kai+char.riku_hyuga+char.mei_arakawa | recipient=pc_wei_tang | Wei completes Team Fujin's first full three-Genin coordination exercise. Because Riku and Mei have already spent chakra earlier in the day and Kai is materially less developed, the exercise emphasizes movement, lanes, objective timing, signals, and ordinary weapons rather than repeated high-output techniques. Riku and Mei must initially reduce pace and simplify their patterns for Kai to remain integrated. Kai performs better when given one immediate timing task at a time and can use his sword pressure inside openings created by the other two. The trio finishes with clearer role spacing than it began, but Kai remains the limiting member and no permanent team doctrine or integer capability increase is created.
